messages.content: Explain why the Moon appears to go through phases. Answer in two to four sentences of plain prose.

message.content: The Moon appears to go through phases because of its orbit around Earth and the changing angles at which sunlight reflects off its surface. As the Moon moves, different portions of its sunlit side become visible from Earth, creating the cycle of phases from New Moon to Full Moon and back. This happens because the Moon does not produce its own light but reflects sunlight, and Earth’s perspective changes as the Moon orbits.
